accepted_review_findings:
[reviewer finding R1, low] F01 is a source_fact that says 'w_{j,i} is the real weight from j in pa(i) to i' and cites source Sec. 2 / Eq. 1. The source's Eq. (1) prose actually writes w_{i,j} for the edge j -> i. That conflicts with the source's own later usage (App. A, Theorems 3/5, Algorithm 2), where w_{j,i} or w_{i,j} with i in pa(j) denotes the edge from the first index to the second. The facts silently adopt the consistent later convention. That is the right reading, but it is presented as what the cited paragraph says, without a correction label, while every other erratum (M03-M07) is labelled. The private rubric gives facts precedence over the sources only 'wherever a fact records a corrected reading (M03-M07)'. A judge who checks Eq. (1) in the source could therefore penalise a solver who correctly follows F01.
Required repair: Add a labelled correction/notation note, either as a new M-fact or as a sentence inside F01 marked as a maintainer normalisation. It should state that the source's Eq. (1) prose writes w_{i,j} for the weight from j in pa(i) to i, which is inconsistent with its later usage, and that the facts uniformly use w_{j,i} = weight of edge j -> i, citing both source locations (B2). Extend the rubric's precedence sentence to cover this notation note. No other fact needs to change, because F09-F13 and F18-F26 already use the adopted convention consistently.

[reviewer finding R2, low] The public contract forbids stating 'experimental or empirical findings of any kind' (task.md Scope limits; M08; output_contract). It also marks F27 as required, and F27's content is an empirical demonstration: data generated from two non-forest systems, with differing estimated covariance matrices. F25 also gives figure values whose computation mode (closed form or sampled) is unknown, though M08's 'numbers in this sheet' wording does cover F25's numbers. A literal reading leaves the solver unable to both cite F27 and obey the 'any kind' prohibition. The private rubric applies a different, looser test ('measured results ... not in the facts is an error'). The public and private requirements therefore disagree, and a solver following the public wording has to guess how to present F27.
Required repair: In M08, in the task.md Scope limits and in the output_contract requirement, state explicitly that the non-forest counterexample in F27 and the illustrative covariance values in F25 are permitted and should be presented as reported in the facts. For F27, that means stating that the source reports the two non-forest systems yield different estimated covariance matrices, with no new numbers. All other empirical or experimental findings stay excluded. Use the same wording in rubric Criterion 4 so that the public and private tests match.
